root_cause.text: The `ti_am335x_tsc` driver’s `titsc_config_wires()` validation used an off-by-one bounds check on `wire_order[i]`, allowing the value `ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins)` to pass and later be used as an out-of-bounds index into the 4-element `config_pins` array.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (WARN_ON(wire_order[i] > ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins)))` to `if (WARN_ON(wire_order[i] >= ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins)))`, and the CVE description states that `wire_order[i] == ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins)` was previously accepted, causing out-of-bounds access in `config_pins[wire_order[i]]`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the wire-order bounds check to correctly reject out-of-range pin indices.
intent_record.what: In `titsc_config_wires()`, the bounds check for `wire_order[i]` changed from `wire_order[i] > ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins)` to `wire_order[i] >= ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins)`.
intent_record.how: This tightens the array index validation so values equal to the array size are now rejected instead of being treated as valid, preventing an out-of-bounds access when `wire_order[i]` is used to index `config_pins`.

grouping_result.intent: Fix the wire-order bounds check to correctly reject out-of-range pin indices.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the off-by-one wire-order bounds check in titsc_config_wires(), which is the root cause of the out-of-bounds access on config_pins.

candidates.rationale: This is the off-by-one validation bug: using '>' instead of '>=' allows wire_order[i] to equal ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins), which later becomes an out-of-bounds index into the 4-element config_pins array.

vuln_statements.explanation: This bounds check is off by one: it rejects values greater than ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins) but still permits equality, allowing wire_order[i] to be 4 for a 4-element array and later be used as an out-of-bounds index into config_pins.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable logic is present in `titsc_config_wires()`. The validation checks `if (WARN_ON(wire_order[i] > ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins)))`, which is an off-by-one upper bound check. Since `config_pins` has 4 elements, allowing `wire_order[i] == ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins)` means value 4 can pass validation and then be used immediately as `bit_cfg = config_pins[wi_order];`, which is an out-of-bounds index. There is no fix here because the comparison is still `>` instead of the correct `>=`, and nothing else prevents the invalid index before the array access.
